title: Guidance for building automatic SMS replies with Automations
summary: The Automations and SMS docs now show how to auto-reply to an inbound SMS, check the number can send, and filter out opt-out and help keywords.
body_markdown:
[Send messages in an automation](https://bird.com/docs/guides/automations/messages#sms) now documents a complete pattern for auto-replying to an inbound SMS: start from an **Incoming SMS** trigger, map the reply's recipient to the incoming sender, and choose the receiving number as the reply's sender, noting that a number can accept inbound SMS without being eligible to send outbound. It also covers using a trigger filter to scope replies to one receiving number and to exclude opt-out and help keywords, so a` STOP` or` HELP` reply doesn't trigger your general acknowledgement. The[SMS overview](https://bird.com/docs/guides/sms/overview) now links to this pattern as the no-code way to handle replies.


Also clarified in the same guide:


- The WhatsApp messaging step can respond to incoming messages, but built-in steps can't label a WhatsApp conversation or assign it to a teammate, that's still a dashboard action under[WhatsApp conversations](https://bird.com/docs/guides/whatsapp/conversations#keep-the-teams-work-organized) .
- The failure path on a send step now explicitly covers sends blocked by your workspace's[send limits](https://bird.com/docs/guides/automations/send-limits) , not just channel rejections.
